curr_de1dcd0ffd.full_pdf_text:
The Inspiring Life of Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam was born on 15 October 1931 in Rameswaram, a small
town in Tamil Nadu, India. He grew up in a humble family and learned the values
of hard work, honesty, and kindness from his parents. As a child, he helped his
family by distributing newspapers while continuing his studies with great
determination. His love for learning and science led him to become an aerospace
scientist, and he played an important role in India’s space and missile
development programmes. Because of his contributions, he became widely
known as the “Missile Man of India.” In 2002, he became the 11th President of
India, serving the country with humility and inspiring millions of young people to
dream big, work hard, and use their knowledge to help others. Even after his
presidency, he continued to teach and encourage students. Dr. Kalam passed
away on 27 July 2015 while delivering a lecture to students, doing what he loved
most. His life reminds us that great achievements can begin with simple dreams,
sincere effort, and a strong desire to serve our nation.

1. Numbers and Operations
Remember
• In 48,326, the digit 8 in the thousands place means 8,000.
• Addition puts amounts together. Subtraction finds the difference.
• Multiplication is repeated addition. Division shares equally.
Let’s practise
1. Write 63,405 in words.
2. What is the value of 7 in 27,914?
3. 3,468 + 2,157 = __________
4. 8,000 − 3,675 = __________
5. 246 × 6 = __________
6. 936 ÷ 9 = __________
Quick check: Estimate 398 + 204 by rounding to the nearest hundred.

topics.concept_summary:
Class 5 Math Mini Book • Page 3
2. Fractions
A fraction shows equal parts of a whole. In 3/4, the 3 is the numerator (parts counted) and the 4 is
the denominator (equal parts in total).
Examples
• 1/2 means one of two equal parts.
• 2/4 is equal to 1/2.
• If a pizza has 8 equal slices and you eat 3, you ate 3/8.
Let’s practise
1. Write the fraction for 5 shaded parts out of 8 equal parts: ______
2. Which is larger: 1/3 or 1/2? ______
3. Fill in the blank: 2/6 = 1/____
4. A chocolate bar has 10 equal pieces. Riya eats 4. What fraction is left? ______
Draw a rectangle and divide it into 4 equal parts. Shade 3 parts to show 3/4.
Drawing space:

topics.concept_summary:
Class 5 Math Mini Book • Page 4
3. Shapes, Measurement and Word Problems
Remember
• Perimeter is the distance around a shape.
• Area is the space inside a flat shape.
• 1 metre = 100 centimetres; 1 kilogram = 1,000 grams.
Let’s practise
1. A rectangle is 8 cm long and 3 cm wide. Find its perimeter.
2. A square has sides of 5 cm. Find its perimeter.
3. Convert 4 m to centimetres.
4. A pencil costs I8. How much do 7 pencils cost?
5. There are 36 students in 4 equal teams. How many students are in each team?
6. Meena reads 12 pages each day for 5 days. How many pages does she read?
I Fun challenge: I am a two-digit number. My tens digit is 4. My ones digit is double my tens digit.
What number am I?
Answers (check after trying)
• Numbers: 1. Sixty-three thousand four hundred five. 2. 7,000. 3. 5,625. 4. 4,325. 5. 1,476. 6. 104. Quick check: about
600.
• Fractions: 1. 5/8. 2. 1/2. 3. 3. 4. 6/10 (or 3/5).
• Shapes/word problems: 1. 22 cm. 2. 20 cm. 3. 400 cm. 4. I56. 5. 9 students. 6. 60 pages. Challenge: 48.
